frame_conflict.why_this_is_not_resolvable_here: RB16-1 forbids inserting a conversion to make the audit pass, and RB16-6's escape hatch applies only when the model output frame is unnamed. It is named: ROBOT_LOCAL_ACTION_COMPONENTS is the sole declaration of what the two output components mean, and it names the mission frame. The two authoritative declarations therefore conflict, and the choice between them is an owner decision, not an implementation detail.

identity_transform.head_saturation_note: the residual head emits tanh(raw) * limits, so a target exactly at a componentwise bound is a limit point the head approaches but never emits. Every strictly interior case round-trips through the frozen bound within float32. This is recorded, not corrected: the bound itself is unchanged.
identity_transform.scope: the world segment only: target builder -> row encode/decode -> frozen model bound -> runtime pre-safety addition. The model stage is a deterministic injected output equal to the target, so this fixture verifies the plumbing under the assumption RB16 could not confirm -- that the model output is world-frame
